explanation: The bees vibrate their flight muscles, heating the ball until the hornet dies, while staying just below the temperature that would kill the bees themselves.

claims.text: Japanese honeybees kill invading giant hornets by surrounding them in a ball and raising its temperature.
Japanese honeybees do not kill hornets by sealing them in wax or by pulling them apart.
The bees generate the heat by vibrating their flight muscles.
The ball becomes hot enough to kill the hornet but stays just below the temperature that would kill the bees.

evidence.restatement: Japanese honeybees engulf an invading giant hornet in a tight ball and raise its temperature until the hornet dies.
They do not seal hornets in wax or tear them apart.
The bees produce the heat by shivering their flight muscles.
The ball reaches about 46 to 47 °C, above the hornet's lethal limit but just under the bees' own lethal limit of roughly 48 to 50 °C.
